doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Cigar makers, Mr. Morial, work songs and Chris Kelly
summary: Albert's father's cigar workers, Mr. Morial, the singing of workers and washerwomen and Chris Kelly's favorite number.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What about your grandmother? Most of the men spoke that Spanish. Because he said he even went to a cigar maker. Most of the cigar makers, yeah, from Cuba. Did you know Mr. Morial was a cigar maker? Mr. Morial, the man's daddy? Worked for my daddy. You knew him? Sure, he used to pick up the technical work all over time. He was a cripple.
Did you know him? I think his name was Ernest. I think Ernest is named that. I never knew about Mr. Morial. 된 stuff
they'd be pumping out. Oh, I never heard that.
They sing, they sing when they be in the other little spike style.
Do you know what they sang?

No, it was their own composition, if you call it a composition. They had their own way of saying things and doing things. It was timed right, it was timed right. It was precision time. Yeah, but I mean, that seems to me that's... You hear things that sound like that's where the footage came from. Well, it's all ties in. Yeah.
And what about women working over wash tubs and doing dishes?
That's the only way they wash was in wash tubs. Yeah, and did they sing?
Well, people always sing. Yeah. You know, I was going back there and I noticed you do that. I'll be washing dishes, but I'm sitting by myself, I sing. Yeah. Well, the same thing.
It's the same thing, I just thought maybe they had some special number. No, it's the same thing, whatever. When they be chopping wood or...
Whatever the person was thinking of, you sing a song. Yeah. Did you ever hear Callous Love? Yeah, and then Chase did the Loveless Love. Mm-hmm. I see.
I think we've talked enough about Chris Kelly.
That was one of Chris Kelly's favorite numbers.
